TOP: Tensorlake npm worm wipes machines if token revoked
Hijacked ccTLDs mint fake Google TLS certs
Cisco NX-OS: five critical Nexus flaws
Agent sandboxes land: AWS Strands Box, Windows containers

P.h: Tensorlake npm worm wipes your home dir if you revoke its token
P.p: tensorlake@0.5.144 steals developer credentials at install and plants a gh-token-monitor service. If the stolen GitHub token is revoked, the service wipes the home directory. Malicious commits pushed to main under a maintainer's name gave the release a valid npm provenance attestation.
P.s: Pin to 0.5.143. Remove ~/.config/gh-token-monitor/ before revoking any token, then rotate every credential the machine held. The worm spreads through victims' npm packages and repos.

items.h: Hijacked ccTLDs yield fake TLS certs for Google
items.d: Attackers took over .gh, .sl and .as, altered DNS and passed CA domain validation. Google blocked the certs in Chrome. Monitor CT logs and publish restrictive CAA records.

items.h: Cisco: five critical NX-OS flaws allow Nexus takeover
items.d: Remote code execution when NX-API, Next Generation OAM or MPLS OAM is enabled. Disable unneeded features and upgrade to a patched version.

items.h: Copilot CLI runs malware via README prompt injection
items.d: 'env curl | env sh' passes the read-only allowlist, so no approval fires. GitHub called it a known issue and declined a bounty.
Targets exposed LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg and Gitea. Mines Monero and hides C2 addresses in GitHub-hosted poetry.

P.h: Agent sandboxes arrive from AWS and Microsoft in one week
P.p: AWS launched Strands Box, an open source sandbox with OS-level containment and Dogwood policies for shell, Python, network egress and MCP tools. Temporal rules cap actions, and secrets are injected at an egress gateway so agents never see real credentials.
P.s: Microsoft made Execution Containers generally available on Windows for the same job. Anthropic also launched OSS Scanner, free vulnerability reports with a proof of concept for open-source maintainers.

P.h: DNS root key rolls today; Let's Encrypt shrinks certs to 64 days
P.p: The DNS root switches to KSK-2024 on October 11. DNSSEC-validating resolvers without the new trust anchor can fail to resolve healthy sites. RFC 8509 sentinel queries test readiness, though an unsupported test is inconclusive.
P.s: Let's Encrypt cuts lifetimes from 90 to 64 days on February 10, 2027, with opt-in testing from October 14. Renewals on hardcoded schedules will break, so move to ACME ARI.
